OS Task Exported Functions

group OS_TASK_Exported_Functions

Variables

bool (*os_alloc_secure_ctx)(uint32_t stack_size)

Allocate secure stack for task switch when trustzone is enabled.

Param stack_size:

Secure stack size, unit: byte.

Return:

Result of allocating secure stack. It return false when there is not enough secure heap to malloc.

bool (*os_task_create)(void **pp_handle, const char *p_name, void (*p_routine)(void*), void *p_param, uint16_t stack_size, uint16_t priority)

Create a new task and add it to the list of tasks that are ready to run.

Example usage 

// Task routine implementation.
void task_routine(void *p_param)
{
    for (;;)
    {
         // Task code goes here.
    }
}

// Task to be created.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint32_t task_param;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       &task_param, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Use the handle to delete the task.
    os_task_delete(p_handle);

    return 0;
}

Param pp_handle:

[out] Pointer used to pass back a handle by which the created task can be referenced.

Param p_name:

[in] A descriptive name for the task.

Param p_routine:

[in] Pointer to task routine function that must be implemented to never return.

Param p_param:

[in] Pointer parameter passed to the task routine function.

Param stack_size:

[in] The size of the task stack that is specified as the number of bytes.

Param priority:

[in] The priority at which the task should run. Higher priority task has a higher priority value.

Retval true:

Task was created successfully and added to the task ready list.

Retval false:

Task failed to be created. It happens when there is not enough heap for task stack.

Return:

The status of the task creation.

bool (*os_task_delete)(void *p_handle)

Remove a task from RTOS's task management. The task being deleted will be removed from RUNNING, READY, or WAITING state.

Example usage 

// Task routine implementation.
void task_routine(void *p_param)
{
    for (;;)
    {
         // Task code goes here.
    }
}

// Task to be created and deleted.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint32_t task_param;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       &task_param, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Use the handle to delete the task.
    os_task_delete(p_handle);

    return 0;
}

Param p_handle:

[in] The handle of the task to be deleted.

Return:

The status of the task deletion. It will always return true.

bool (*os_task_suspend)(void *p_handle)

Suspend the task. The suspended task will not be scheduled and never get any microcontroller processing time.

Example usage 

// Task routine implementation.
void task_routine(void *p_param)
{
    for (;;)
    {
         // Task code goes here.
    }
}

// Task to be created and suspended.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint32_t task_param;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       &task_param, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Use the handle to suspend the created task.
    os_task_suspend(p_handle);

    return 0;
}

Param p_handle:

[in] The handle of the task to be suspended.

Return:

The status of the task suspension. It will always return true.

bool (*os_task_resume)(void *p_handle)

Resume the suspended task.

Example usage 

// Task routine implementation.
void task_routine(void *p_param)
{
    for (;;)
    {
         // Task code goes here.
    }
}

// Task to be suspended and resumed.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint32_t task_param;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       &task_param, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Use the handle to suspend the created task.
    os_task_suspend(p_handle);

    // Resume the suspended task by ourselves.
    os_task_resume(p_handle);
    return 0;
}

Param p_handle:

[in] The handle of the task to be resumed.

Return:

The status of the task resume. It will always return true.

bool (*os_task_yield)(void)

Force a context switch and pass control to the next task that is in ready state.

Example usage 

// Task routine implementation.
void task_routine(void *p_param)
{
    for (;;)
    {
         // Force a context switch
         os_task_yield();
    }
}

// Task to be created.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint32_t task_param;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       &task_param, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

Return:

The status of the task resume. It will always return true.

bool (*os_task_handle_get)(void **pp_handle)

Get the handle of the currently running task.

Example usage 

// Get current task handle.
int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;

    os_task_handle_get(&p_handle);

    return 0;
}

Param pp_handle:

[out] Pointer used to pass back a handle by which the current task can be referenced.

Retval true:

Task handle was obtained successfully.

Retval false:

Task handle failed to get. It happens when pp_handle is NULL.

Return:

The status of getting the current task handle.

bool (*os_task_priority_get)(void *p_handle, uint16_t *p_priority)

Get the priority of the specified task.

Example usage 

int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint16_t priority;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       NULL, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Get the task priority.
    os_task_priority_get(p_handle, &priority);

    return 0;
}

Param p_handle:

[in] The handle of the task to be queried. Passing a NULL handle means querying the priority of the current task.

Param p_priority:

[in] Pointer used to pass back the priority of the task.

Retval true:

Task priority was obtained successfully.

Retval false:

Task priority failed to get. It happens when p_handle is NULL.

Return:

The status of getting the task priority.

bool (*os_task_priority_set)(void *p_handle, uint16_t priority)

Set the priority of the specified task.

Example usage 

int test(void)
{
    void *p_handle = NULL;
    uint16_t priority;

    if (os_task_create(&p_handle, "task", task_routine,
                       NULL, STACK_SIZE, TASK_PRIORITY) == true)
    {
        // Task created successfully.
    }
    else
    {
        // Task failed to create.
        return -1;
    }

    // Use the handle to raise the created task priority.
    os_task_priority_set(p_handle, TASK_PRIORITY + 1);

    // Use a NULL handle to raise the current task priority.
    os_task_priority_set(NULL, TASK_PRIORITY + 1);

    return 0;
}

Param p_handle:

[in] The handle of the task for which the priority is being set. Passing a NULL handle means setting the priority of the current task.

Param priority:

[in] The priority to which the task will be set.

Return:

The status of setting the task priority. It will always return true.
